subject: Anatomy
summary: The sympathetic nervous system (SNS) is a thoracolumbar network that prepares the body for rapid action. It modulates heart rate, vascular tone, and metabolic responses via short‑acting norepinephrine and adrenal catecholamines.

sections.p: The SNS is one half of the autonomic nervous system, originating from spinal cord segments T1–L2. It uses a two‑neuron chain (preganglionic and postganglionic) to reach target organs.
b: Preganglionic fibers are short, myelinated, release acetylcholine.
Postganglionic fibers are long, unmyelinated, release norepinephrine (except sweat glands).
Adrenal medulla acts as a modified sympathetic ganglion.

sections.p: Preganglionic cell bodies lie in the intermediolateral columns of T1‑L2. Their axons exit via ventral roots, join spinal nerves, and enter white rami communicantes.
b: Gray rami = unmyelinated postganglionic fibers to the spinal nerve.

sections.p: Sympathetic chains run bilaterally alongside the vertebral bodies, forming the sympathetic trunk. They communicate via rami communicantes and interganglionic fibers.
b: Cervical ganglia (e.g., superior cervical) supply head and neck.
Thoracic ganglia supply heart, lungs, and upper limbs.
Lumbar ganglia supply lower abdomen and pelvis.

sections.p: The sympathetic trunks receive arterial blood from segmental branches of the aorta (intercostal, lumbar arteries). Venous drainage follows the azygos and lumbar veins.
Preganglionic fibers travel in white rami; postganglionic fibers exit via gray rami to join spinal nerves and reach target organs.
b: Sympathetic fibers to the heart travel via the cardiac plexus.
Fibers to the adrenal medulla synapse directly on chromaffin cells.

sections.p: Activation triggers the ‘fight‑or‑flight’ response: ↑ heart rate, ↑ contractility, vasoconstriction of skin, vasodilation of skeletal muscle, bronchodilation, glycogenolysis, and pupil dilation.
b: β‑adrenergic receptors mediate cardiac ↑output and bronchodilation.

t.b: Is sympathetic tone elevated? High levels support hyperadrenergic states (e.g., pheochromocytoma).
Low HRV indicates reduced parasympathetic balance, often seen in chronic stress or sepsis.

sections.p: Disruption of sympathetic pathways produces characteristic patterns of autonomic loss, while over‑activity leads to hypertension, tachycardia, and hypermetabolism.
b: Spinal cord injury above T6 → loss of sympathetic outflow → neurogenic shock.
Complex regional pain syndrome (CRPS) → sympathetic‑maintained pain.

t.b: Screen for pheochromocytoma; elevated levels confirm catecholamine‑secreting tumor.
Detect neurogenic shock; a drop >20 mmHg systolic on standing suggests autonomic failure.

sections.p: Focus on the pathway, neurotransmitters, and clinical scenarios that test autonomic balance.
b: Adrenal medulla releases epinephrine > norepinephrine into bloodstream.
Loss of sympathetic tone → bradycardia, hypotension, warm extremities.

whenToSeekHelp: Sudden severe hypertension with headache, sweating, palpitations (possible pheochromocytoma crisis).
Unexplained persistent tachycardia with chest pain (risk of myocardial ischemia).
Neurogenic shock after high spinal injury (hypotension, bradycardia).

faq.q: Why does the adrenal medulla release epinephrine more than norepinephrine?
faq.a: Chromaffin cells are innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers; they convert norepinephrine to epinephrine using phenylethanolamine N‑methyltransferase.

faq.q: What distinguishes sympathetic from parasympathetic effects on the heart?
faq.a: Sympathetic ↑heart rate and contractility via β1 receptors; parasympathetic ↓rate via muscarinic receptors.

faq.q: Can a low plasma norepinephrine level be normal?
faq.a: Yes; levels vary with posture and stress. Very low levels in a supine patient may indicate sympathetic failure.

exam: Describe the two‑neuron pathway of the sympathetic nervous system and name the neurotransmitters at each synapse.
Explain how a pheochromocytoma produces its clinical signs and which test confirms the diagnosis.
A patient with a T4 spinal cord injury develops hypotension and bradycardia. Identify the autonomic mechanism and immediate management steps.
